ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure is a transition-state structure, containing two Ar aryl groups, one NC substituent, one negatively charged O, an OH on the right side, and a C-H on the right side; there are also curved arrows in the figure. According to the problem statement, ignore the arrows and exclude all bonds involving hydrogen. Reasoning: The lower-left Ar aryl group is counted as a benzene ring, with 6 internal ring bonds, plus its connecting bond to the central carbon, totaling 7. The upper Ar aryl group is connected to the right-side carbon, likewise having 6 aromatic-ring bonds plus 1 connecting bond, totaling 7. The NC substituent includes its connecting bond to the central carbon and the internal C≡N bond, totaling 2. The remaining core non-hydrogen bonds are: central carbon to O−, central carbon to the right-side carbon, and right-side carbon to the OH oxygen, totaling 3. Exclude the right-side C-H bond and the O-H bond in OH. The total number is 7 + 7 + 2 + 3 = 19.

raw_record.question_text: In the transition-state structure shown in the image, calculate the total number of bonds in the structure, including single, double, and triple bonds but excluding those involving hydrogen. Disregard arrows. Consider all components present in the transition-state structure shown in the image.

method.method_draft: Expand the image into components. For the lower-left Ar group: 6 aryl-ring bonds + 1 attachment to the central carbon = 7. For the upper Ar group attached to the right carbon: 6 aryl-ring bonds + 1 attachment = 7. For the NC substituent: count the drawn attachment to the central carbon plus the internal C≡N bond = 2. For the remaining drawn core bonds: central carbon to O−, central carbon to right carbon, and right carbon to OH oxygen = 3. Exclude the right C-H bond and the O-H bond in OH, and ignore arrows. Sum 7 + 7 + 2 + 3 = 19.
